reviewed_scope: Current PR metadata, body synchronization, base/head SHAs, complete commit/file delta, and exact-head CI

decision.rationale: The direct native mapping, F6 synchronization, configured tests, and exact-head CI pass, but the new package-owned failure is missing from the public routing tuple and contradictory or malformed unsupported evidence can still authorize a second desktop mutation.

summary: The latest remediation correctly distinguishes definite unsupported native results from uncertain outcomes and synchronizes the lifecycle records. Two public-boundary gaps remain: tuple-based callers cannot classify the new package failure, and the WeChat recovery predicate can trust contradictory or malformed no-effect evidence and execute a second mutation. The PR must not merge until PRR-025 and PRR-026 are resolved.

findings.title: New package failure is missing from the stable routing tuple
findings.observation: client.py emits failureKind=accessibility_action_unsupported for native -25206 and -25205, but errors.py does not declare that value in COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS.
findings.trigger: A direct accessibility_action receives native -25206 or -25205 and an application routes the result through the documented public failure tuple.
findings.impact: A legitimate package-owned result is exposed as unknown to callers following the stable routing contract, which can select an incorrect generic recovery path or reject the result.

evidence.description: A real ComputerUseClient fixture returned failureKind=accessibility_action_unsupported with declared=false.
The package README, docs/api.md, and errors.py module contract describe COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS as stable package-owned failure routing.
An explicit membership assertion failed with exit code 1 while the existing regex-based contract test passed because it does not scan generated-script fail literals.

findings.remediation: Declare a stable ACCESSIBILITY_ACTION_UNSUPPORTED constant, include its value in COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS, and test real -25206 and -25205 observations against the public tuple.
findings.verification: Both native unsupported observations belong to COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS, and package/root, preflight, wheel/API smoke, and exact-head CI pass.

findings.title: Contradictory unsupported evidence can still trigger a second mutation
findings.observation: The recovery exception checks the new failure kind and collected non-empty string effects but ignores contradictory nativeErrorCode values and present malformed or empty duplicate effects.
findings.trigger: A compatible, version-skewed, or partially malformed backend reports accessibility_action_unsupported and one actionEffect=none while another field reports -25204, missing or inconsistent action evidence, or an invalid duplicate effect.
findings.impact: WeChat can execute a coordinate, selector, or Return fallback after an action whose native outcome is unknown, causing an unintended second desktop mutation.

evidence.description: A ToolObservation carrying the new failure kind, none effects, and nativeErrorCode=-25204 made the predicate return true and _click_node_phase execute a click.
The inverse fail-closed assertion exited 1; operations were accessibility_action followed by click.
Replacing a nested duplicate effect with an object still made the predicate return true because the malformed value was ignored.

findings.remediation: Validate one complete unsupported/no-effect proof at the trust boundary, reject every present malformed or contradictory value, and define the required action and native-code consistency without weakening normal no-replay paths.
findings.verification: Counterexamples for -25204 paired with unsupported/none, wrong action-code pairing, missing required proof, and invalid or contradictory duplicates execute zero fallback; valid AXPress/-25206 and AXSetFocus/-25205 still execute exactly one.

findings.title: Definite unsupported native actions were treated as unknown mutations
findings.observation: The direct backend now emits none only for AXPress/-25206 and AXSetFocus/-25205 and emits unknown for other native errors.
findings.trigger: Native Accessibility returns a definite unsupported or uncertain error code.
findings.impact: Valid definite no-effect results retain one fallback while uncertain direct-backend results do not replay.

evidence.description: Package and cross-package tests cover both definite unsupported cases and seven unsafe modes; ten iterations produced 70 zero-replay unsafe outcomes.

findings.remediation: Completed for the supported production path; preserve the direct mapping while resolving PRR-026.
findings.verification: Well-formed direct-backend results and the existing unsafe modes pass package and cross-package tests.
